title: The bait mode's monitor is Isao's camera, and the seat's MK-9 no longer speaks in Isao's voice
context: Owner, 2026-10-09: "the camera still says 'ground truth/impact', it is not the POV of Isao" (he approved the proposal: the bottom-right monitor becomes a camera on Isao, a quadcopter that can fly away while looking straight at the creature) and "while in this mode, we should disable the 'nuke launched' lines, since they are the same voice as ISAO it is confusing." The read-only investigation (scratchpad isao-cam-investigation.md) found the monitor's API could aim anywhere but capped the lens at 30 degrees, and that the seat's only voice on an MK-9 was game-seat.js's launchHeavy copying gunship-rig.js's isaoSpeak('mk9_release', { force: true }). Bait mode only; the tank mode and the game are unchanged.
outcome: (1) src/fx/story-monitor.js takes one optional optic field, `fov` (degrees, vertical), replacing the 3-30 degree lens when given (`optic.fov ?? <the clamp>`); td-tab.js and gunshipOptic() pass none, so the game's monitor is unchanged (--gunship green, its GROUND TRUTH · IMPACT and MK-9 · ROUND IN FLIGHT assertions included). (2) src/labs/boss/bait.js: Isao's body faces the creature's centre (`face`, eased at the autopilot's 3 rad/s turn) while the domain's `heading` stays his flight's (state().facing); `cam(aim)` puts the eye on his nose, 1.5 m ahead of his origin along the facing and 0.3 m under it (his body behind and above the lens), looking along the facing's azimuth at the true pitch, never steeper than 80 degrees from the horizon. The monitor keeps the planet's up, so a look straight down would leave the picture's roll to the look's azimuth, which flips as a hop crosses over the creature; with the azimuth the eased facing, the picture turns at 3 rad/s at most. (3) src/labs/boss/game-seat.js feeds the monitor { from, pos, lift: 0, fov: 70, label: 'ISAO · CAM' } in game units each frame while he flies (boss-tab.js's aim: the creature's mass centre 2 m up); `monitorCam(false)` (the lab's I, a capture listener before the seat's, like R and C) gives back the game's GROUND TRUTH impact view and its MK-9 feed, and with him gone the game's view comes back by itself; state().monitor reports the label, the camera drawn and the monitor's render ms by view. (4) The seat's MK-9 release says nothing (no mk9_release take; the release clunk, motor and blast stay; the chatter director's bait_nuke_careful and bait_nuke_face stay); the unused voice sink call in the seat went with it. MEASURED (--boss-bait, headless, 1440x900 dpr 1): over 10 s of lab clock the camera was 1.53 m from Isao's origin, at most 4.06-4.9 degrees off the creature's mass centre, his body a median 0.3-0.7 degrees off the creature while his flight heading was a median 93-148 degrees off it; through a forced hop (399-429 frames) the picture turned at most 3.83-3.97 degrees a frame while the bearing to the creature swung up to 19-41 degrees a frame, the pitch clamp reached (79.9); the monitor's render call (JS, the canvas copy's sync included) averaged 0.50-0.62 ms a frame on the GROUND TRUTH view and 0.32-0.34 ms on Isao's camera (the investigation's frame-time measure: about +1 ms for the wide view); one MK-9 release in the bait mode added no mk9_release entry to Isao's voice log while 35 bait lines were in it. Also: the close call's caption in chatter.js matched to its re-recorded take ('That was too close!', commit 06c5112b; the chatter test failed after 0e200304).
alternatives: Isao's camera except while an MK-9 falls (the game's mesh priority; rejected: the four seconds of the fall are when the gunner most needs Isao's view, and the MK-9 is in his frame as it comes down)
An `up` field for the monitor to hold the roll (rejected: one new field in the game's module only; the pitch clamp and the eased azimuth live in the lab)
Hiding Isao's mesh for the monitor's pass (not needed: the nose eye has his body behind and above it)
evidence: node --check on every edited file; npm test, npm run check, npm run build green
from an APFS snapshot, sequentially, one headless Chrome (memory WARN on swap): --boss-friends, --boss-bait (with boss-bait-friends), --boss, --gunship green

--boss-bait additions: ISAO · CAM throughout, the eye within 3 m of Isao and the look within 10 degrees of the creature's centre, the body facing it (median under 5 degrees), I to GROUND TRUTH · IMPACT and back, the monitor ms by view logged, the picture turning under 10 degrees a frame through a forced hop, no mk9_release in Isao's voice log over the bait mode's MK-9 releases (the MK-9 screenshot now on the I view)

flaky on the tree before the change as well: the earlier-pursuit gap run's keep (the unchanged tree: 18.2, 17.8, then 16.0 against the 17 bound, a failure, in three runs; with the change: 16.0, 15.8, 16.2, 18.5, 16.6, 18.x in six runs, four failures; the planner is untouched, the body's facing and the monitor's view do not feed it) and the far-side 40 mm's hits (0 of 32 in one run, 1 to 3 otherwise); the full suite passed on the seventh run with the change. Four failures in six is more than the unchanged tree's one in three: worth a look if it persists
